how: Each protocol as its source states it, read 2026-10-18: the operations it covers, the distance it counts an earthquake within, and each magnitude level with the action it requires. Where the regulator's own document was read it is cited; where only a summary of it was found, the summary is cited and marked secondary. The program shows which level an earthquake would reach; it never decides that an operation caused it, and a site's own permit conditions govern over anything here.

protocols.name: British Columbia - Kiskatinaw Seismic Monitoring and Mitigation Area
protocols.document: BC Oil and Gas Commission Order 18-90-001 (Amendment #2), Kiskatinaw Seismic Monitoring and Mitigation Area Special Project Order, 16 April 2021, with its guidance
protocols.monitoring: an accelerometer within 3 km of the trajectory; a real-time array with a magnitude of completeness of 1.5 within 5 km

levels.action: pause the causing well for 12 hours
suspend every well on the pad for at least 5 calendar days
suspend hydraulic fracturing on the pad immediately, for at least 5 calendar days

cluster.action: five or more events felt or of magnitude 2.5 or more within 72 hours: the Commission may require a 24-hour pause, a technical conference and a revised completion program

protocols.name: Alberta - Subsurface Order No. 2 (Duvernay, Fox Creek)
protocols.jurisdiction: Alberta (the Duvernay zone in the order's area)
protocols.document: Alberta Energy Regulator, Subsurface Order No. 2, 19 February 2015
protocols.monitoring: sufficient to detect a 2.0 ML event within 5 km of any affected well; an induced seismicity plan on site before completion

levels.action: report immediately to the AER and carry out the induced seismicity plan
report immediately; cease hydraulic fracturing at the affected well and return it to a safe state; resume only with the AER's written consent

protocols.name: Oklahoma - completion operations near anomalous seismicity
protocols.document: Oklahoma Corporation Commission, Oil and Gas Conservation Division, notice to operators: action following anomalous seismic activity apparently not related to injection into the Arbuckle (version stamp OGCD_v_20161223)

levels.action: the Commission reviews the completion notices within 2 km and calls the operator; the operator applies its own mitigation and may continue
pause stimulation for at least 6 hours; a technical conference with the Commission before resuming on a revised procedure
suspend stimulation; a technical conference within 48 hours; resume only on an agreed revised procedure

protocols.name: Ohio - permit conditions for horizontal wells near faults or seismicity
protocols.jurisdiction: Ohio (new permits within 3 miles of a known fault or of seismic activity above magnitude 2.0)
protocols.document: Ohio Department of Natural Resources permit conditions announced April 2014, as summarised by Vorys (April 2014) and Babst Calland
protocols.radius_from: the permit's own conditions (the summaries name no distance for the trigger)
protocols.monitoring: sensitive seismic monitors on the site

levels.action: pause completion while the cause is investigated; if a probable connection to hydraulic fracturing is found, all completion operations are suspended

protocols.name: Texas - Response Plan to Seismic Events
protocols.document: Railroad Commission of Texas, Oil and Gas Division, Response Plan to Seismic Events in Texas, 31 January 2022
protocols.radius_from: the seismic event of significance (a larger radius around deep wells)

levels.action: a seismic event of significance: data requests to disposal operators, inspections, a possible Seismic Response Area with a curtailment plan; for hydraulic fracturing, voluntary: pause 24 hours or skip stages within 9.08 km
